Inglewood, California
  April 11, 2023

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  April 11, 2023, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
  Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the hour
  of 2:03 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
  presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present: Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts,
  Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority
  Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent: None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any item
  on the Agendas, other than the public hearing.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) spoke concerning a matter not on the Agenda, and was advised
  to speak towards the end of the meeting to address his concerns.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by Council
  Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the demands
  presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated April 7, 2023,
  in the amount of $7,020,586.47 are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers
  that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  RESOLUTION NO. 23-84 ADOPTED – INGLEWOOD TRANSIT CONNECTOR
  PROJECT, AS MODIFIED EXEMPT FROM THE CALIFORNIA
  ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT; RESOULTION NO. 23-85 ADOPTED –
  APPROVED MODIFICATION OF THE INGLEWOOD TRANSIT CONNECTOR
  PROJECT, A LOCALLY PREFERRED ALTERNATIVE FOR THE FEDERAL
  TRANSIT ADMINISTRATION. Staff report dated April 11, 2023, was presented
  recommending that the Mayor and Council Members adopt a resolution affirming that the
  Inglewood Transit Connector Project, as modified, is statutorily exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act; approving and adopting the first Addendum to the Certified
  Final Environmental Impact Report SCH #2018071034 for the Project; approving and
  adopting the California Environmental Quality Act Findings of Fact; and approving and
  adopting revisions to Project Design Feature CUL-1 included in the Mitigation Monitoring
  and Reporting Program for the Project.

  1
 April 11, 2023

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Adopt Resolution No. 23-84 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD AFFIRMING THAT THE INGLEWOOD TRANSIT
  CONNECTOR PROJECT  AS MODIFIED IS STATUTORILY
  EXEMPT FROM THE CALIFORNIA  ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY
  ACT; APPROVING AND ADOPTING THE FIRST ADDENDUM TO THE
  CERTIFIED FINAL ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT REPORT SCH #2018071034
  FOR THE PROJECT; APPROVING AND ADOPTING THE CALIFORNIA
  ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT FINDINGS OF FACT; AND
  APPROVING AND ADOPTING REVISONS TO PROJECT DESIGN FEATURE
  CUL-1 INCLUDED IN THE MITIGATION MONITORING AND REPORTING
  PROGRAM FOR THE PROJECT

  and; 2) Adopt Resolution No. 23-85 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD APPROVING MODIFIED PROJECT AS THE
  INGLEWOOD TRANSIT CONNECTOR PROJECT LOCALLY
  PREFERRED ALTERNATIVE FOR THE PURPOSES OF THE FEDERAL
  TRANSIT ADMINISTRATION AND APPROVING REVISIONS TO THE
  DESIGN STANDARDS AND GUIDELINES FOR THE INGLEWOOD
  TRANSIT CONNECTOR PROJECT

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes:  None.

 132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claims Pursuant to Government Code Section 913:
  1) Tameka Burnett for alleged personal injury; dangerous condition at Edward Vincent
  Park on August 6, 2022.
  2) Roland Burts for alleged vehicle damage; fallen tree on February 14, 2023.
  3) Rafael Espinoza for alleged tire damage; pothole on January 16, 2023.
  4) R C Jones for alleged personal injury; vehicle collision with an MTA bus on June 18,
  2022.
  5) Ricardo Lara for alleged tire damage; pothole on January 16, 2023.
  B. Reject Late Claim Pursuant to Government Code Section 913:
  1) First Evangelical Lutheran for alleged personal injury; water leak on August 25, 2022.

  It was moved by Council Member Padilla, and seconded by Council Member Morales that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Reject claims listed as A-1 through A-5; and 2) Reject
  late claim listed as B-1. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes:  None.

 178  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – AMERICAN BIKE PATROL SERVICES (ABPS).
  Staff report dated April 11, 2023, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council
  Members authorize payment of an invoice submitted by American Bike Patrol Services
  (ABPS) for bicycle parts and services.

  It was moved by Council Member Padilla, and seconded by Council Member Morales that
  the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the total amount of $1,579.25. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes:  None.

  2
 April 11, 2023

 178  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – MEDICO HEALTHCARE LINEN SERVICE
  (MEDICO). Staff report dated April 11, 2023, was presented recommending that the
  Mayor and Council Members authorize payment of invoices submitted by Medico
  Healthcare Linen Service (Medico) for linen rental services.

  It was moved by Council Member Padilla, and seconded by Council Member Morales that
  the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the total amount of $3,431.09. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes:  None.

 178  PATRICK LEAHY BULLETPROOF VEST PARTNERSHIP (BVP) FUNDS
  ACCEPTED. Staff report dated April 11, 2023, was presented recommending that the
  Mayor and Council Members accept Fiscal Year 2022 Patrick Leahy Bulletproof Vest
  Partnership (BVP) Funds.

  It was moved by Council Member Padilla, and seconded by Council Member Morales that
  the City Council does hereby accept funds in the amount of $8,453.90. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes:  None.

 178  CHIEF OF POLICE REPORT OUTLINING PROPOSED TOW FEE DECREASE
  – RECEIVED AND FILED; DECREASE OF FEES FOR CITY REFERRED TOWS
  AND DAILY STORAGE FEE APPROVED; AND INCLUSION OF NEW FEES
  (RATES) IN THE CITY’S MASTER FEE SCHEDULE APPROVED. Staff report
  dated April 11, 2023, was presented outlining the following proposed tow fee decrease by
  the Chief of Police:
  1. Decrease the fee for City referred tows by $5.35 from the current rate of $179.35
  to $174.00; and
  2. Decrease the daily storage fee by $7.16 from the current rate of $57.00 to $49.84.

  It was moved by Council Member Padilla, and seconded by Council Member Morales that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Receive and file the proposed tow fee decrease; and 2)
  Include new rates in the City’s Master Fee Schedule when applicable. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes:  None.

 183  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – ADOPTION OF THE RELOCATION PLAN FOR
  THE INGLEWOOD TRANSIT CONNECTOR PROJECT. The City Clerk announced
  the next schedule matter was a public hearing to consider adoption of the Relocation Plan
  for the Inglewood Transit Connector Project, notice had been given in the time, form, and
  manner as required by law, an affidavit was on file, and communications were received.

  The City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson received communications via email from Sikivu
  Hutchinson, Marvin McCoy, and David Nottingham who all opposed the Adoption of the
  Relocation Plan for the Inglewood Transit Connector Project.

  Mayor Butts ordered the communications received and filed.

  Artie Fields, City Manager presented the staff report dated April 11, 2023.

  3
 April 11, 2023

  Lisa Trifiletti, Project Manager for the Inglewood Transit Connector (ITC) Project,
  presented an update on what the Inglewood Transit Connector's addendum included and how
  the relocation plan had been modified to reflect the project's modifications. She reviewed the
  ITC's reasoning, including the critical first-last mile gap between the K-Line  and the sports
  and entertainment center. She stated that the ITC was home to future  housing growth and
  employment. This would include work with the Clippers, Intuit  Dome, and the robust activity
  at the KIA Forum and SoFi Stadium, potentially holding up  to 450 events annually. In
  addition, she outlined what the ITC achieved, such as creating  thousands of jobs, enhancing
  mobility, and reducing traffic congestion. Lisa emphasized concern about having all the major
  and minor arterial streets congested during events and  taking hours to get through traffic.
  She also stated that they have been working for over  five years on a comprehensive master
  plan that entails more than the ITC. They have  looked at improving transit across the board
  under the City’s direction.

  She added that they have worked closely with the Planning Department, the Public
  Works Department, Metro, and South Bay COG on improving transit.

  Furthermore, she discussed what was being done besides the ITC, including getting
  residents ready for transit opportunities. They looked at an intelligent transportation system
  that synchronizes traffic lights and connects to the City of Los Angeles, Cal Trans freeway
  on and off ramps, and the county. Lisa also stated that they had spearheaded IRide to do
  micro-mobility and IPark and Go, another initiative the city has taken to get people out of
  their cars on days of the events and improve the bicycle network. Lisa also discussed ITC
  being the centerpiece of three stations. One of the stations at Market Street, one across the
  street from the KIA Forum, and one across from SoFi Stadium at Hardy to alleviate
  neighborhood and air quality congestion.

  In closing, Lisa reviewed reducing greenhouse gas emissions in the area, creating local job
  opportunities, the positive transformation of Inglewood, and the project's benefits. This
  included the achievement of $765 million in federal, state, and local funds. She discussed
  Vons Supermarket's current location and the well-designed, fully enclosed, integrated
  maintenance facility at the first stop. She also mentioned that the acquisition of Manchester,
  Vons, the gas station, and neighboring retail space would no longer be needed. Finally, she
  said the 12-foot shift would allow parking reconfiguration on Market Street.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council on the Public Hearing.

  Steve Cotton, a local small business owner, spoke in favor of the ITC Project. He stated
  that change was inevitable and would happen. He also stated there have been many changes
  in the City of Inglewood, and they must learn how to ride the wave. He mentioned
  that SoFi and other prominent organizations like the Clippers took time to reach small
  businesses such as his. He also mentioned that the big organizations included small
  businesses in community engagements, projects for people experiencing homelessness,
  and giving back.

  Furthermore, he stated that people should consider the bigger picture when referring to the
  people mover. Mr. Cotton noted that the people mover could bring people to and from
  small businesses to shop and eat. When travelers land at LAX, they can get on the transit,
  visit local companies, and get souvenirs. Finally, he said people would walk away, saying
  they had a chance to visit Inglewood, California.

  Owen Smith, Miracle Theatre owner, spoke in favor of the ITC Project. He stated that the
  theatre has become a cultural event theatre that hosts concerts and comedy shows and
  serves the community's needs. He mentioned the Rams football team before announcing
  SoFi Stadium being their home and the embrace of change. He stated that evolution is  about
  change, and the ITC is the latest representation of change. He also said they would
  embrace this change because it would bring business to Market Street. Mr. Smith
  recommended establishing a business owner association that helps engage with new
  developments.

  4
 April 11, 2023

  Speaker (Name Unknown) welcomed Council Member Gloria Gray. She stated that the
  project had bidders, but the community didn’t know what type of train it would be. She
  addressed ITC's projected amount but questioned the project's actual cost. Additionally, she
  mentioned the K-Line not having many riders and challenged the idea of having many  riders
  come for 1.6 miles. Finally, she asked whether the project would serve the community.

  Mayor Butts closed the public comment portion at the hour of 2:21 p.m.

  After discussion, it was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council
  Member Padilla that the City Council does hereby adopt the Relocation Plan. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes:  None.

  REPORTS – CITY MANAGER. The City Manager, Artie Fields, welcomed Council
  Member Gloria Gray to the City of Inglewood Family. He also presented her with
  flowers from him and the Department Heads.

  Council Member Morales left the dais at the hour of 2:42 p.m.

  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. The City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson, welcomed Council
  Member Gloria Gray to the dais and said she looked forward to working with her. She
  also reported attending the Tree Planting Event hosted by Aspiration & the Los Angeles
  Clippers at Edward Vincent Park. She stated she learned a lot about trees and touched the
  soil. The City Clerk reminded women to register for the Women Rock Empowerment
  Summit hosted by herself and Council Member Faulk. Finally, she requested that the City
  Council Meeting be closed in memory of her dad, Bibe Lorenzo Phillips, Sr.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Pedro (Last Name Unknown) spoke concerning the changes in the City of Inglewood,
  such as the Clippers Arena and the Daniel Freeman Hospital being changed into
  condominiums. He also stated that Inglewood is not being erased but replaced with good
  things. Additionally, he addressed the Inglewood Transit Connector cost and the funding gap.
  He questioned whether the gap would be filled with grants or bonds because it  wasn’t made
  clear in communications via Facebook or Instagram. Finally, he asked if a measure was in effect
  that only grants would be used for the project.

  Council Member Morales returned to the dais at the hour of 2:44 p.m.

  Phyllis Weatherspoon spoke about the need for more electric car charging stations
  downtown. She asked if a budget had been established for the ITC.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) congratulated the great City of Inglewood members. He stated
  that he was repeating what he said earlier regarding the city of champions, which is what
  the Lakers were. He also indicated that he hoped the Clippers would be champions and
  expressed his displeasure with the name. He also expressed his displeasure with the
  Clippers owner and requested a name change.

  Sandra Wilson spoke concerning her experience as a homeowner in the Inglewood
  Crossroads. She stated that Lisa Trifiletti was kind enough with her team to explain
  everything going on. She spoke on behalf of the Inglewood Crossroads owner to thank them
  for keeping Vons Supermarket in its current location.

  5
 April 11, 2023

  Nick Tolson thanked the Council for everything that has happened in Inglewood. He
  stated that he has always been proud to be a native of Inglewood, and it’s great to see  people
  who are pleased to visit. He mentioned purchasing a home in the city and discussed  his
  accomplishments. Additionally, he stated that he was ready to bring his talents back to his
  hometown. He asked if any public-private partnerships existed on any  City-owned property.
  Furthermore, he mentioned meeting the Mayor and thanked Emory  for connecting him
  with Maria in administration. Finally, he said he wanted to introduce  himself in person.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in memory of Bibe Lorenzo Phillips, Sr., father of City Clerk Aisha L.
  Thompson and Dorothy R. Davidson at the hour of 3:11 p.m.

  Approved this 1st day of August, 2023.

  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk
